title: Coordinators look weak on solo benchmarks yet multiply output across complementary specialists
text: Organizations create 'mosaic intelligence' by combining specialists whose capabilities are jagged in different directions (yielding a 32% performance advantage for complementary pairings over random pairs in the authors’ 100-person, six-domain quiz). Judged by solo task benchmarks, a pure coordinator appears average at every execution skill, yet inside a team skilled coordination reduces handoff friction, raises specialist productivity, and expands the firm’s optimal scale.
qualification: Empirical quiz evidence comes from a stylized 100-participant six-domain task rather than an enterprise workplace study; the scaling curve model abstracts away from internal organizational politics and bureaucratic overhead.

public_locator.value: Inside a team, however, a skilled coordinator eases handoff friction across colleagues, enables the team to grow larger without losing focus, and makes every coder and writer noticeably more productive.
